title: Why Golf Balls Have Dimples ⛳ #shorts
description:
A dimpled golf ball can fly nearly twice as far as a smooth one. As a ball flies, air flows around it and peels off the back, leaving a swirling low-pressure wake that drags it backward. On a smooth ball the air separates early and the wake is huge. Dimples trip a thin turbulent layer of air at the surface that clings to the ball longer, so the air leaves later, the wake shrinks and drag drops. With backspin, the dimples also help create lift. Golfers discovered this by accident: old scuffed balls flew farther than new smooth ones, and by 1905 dimpled balls were being made.
